title: Investigate and fix cross-deployment token accounting divergence for multi-tenant customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Several enterprise customers reported mismatches between: (A) invoice token counts from Redwood Console and (B) their own client-side metering logs. Discrepancies are observed in Hosted and Dedicated customers and appear sporadically for Private deployments with older runtime agents. Reported symptoms: invoices are overcharging (up to +18%) or undercounting (-6%) compared to customer logs. This ticket drives an investigation into the end-to-end metering pipeline, fixes for root causes, and a short-term mitigation path to stop new divergences.
impact_summary: High-value customers raised support escalations; at least two have paused bill payments pending reconciliation. Financial exposure estimate: up to ~$90k in disputed usage for the last billing cycle across 3 customers. Reputational risk and churn if not resolved before next invoice window.
observed_patterns: Discrepancies spike during multi-request streaming sessions (long-lived chat sessions with streaming tokens)
Dedicated pools show higher overcount rates when autoscaling events occur within a minute of heavy prefix caching hits
Private deployments with runtime < 1.20 report undercounting (missing final tokens) in verbose logs
Difference correlates with requests that use function-calling + tool responses (structured output)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a multi-turn chat scenario with streaming enabled and function-calling enabled (e.g., customer-provided integration).
2) Produce concurrent long sessions (10-30 users) hitting the same model variant with KV caching enabled and the same customer API key.
3) Force an autoscale event on Dedicated pool (or restart runtime agent for Private) mid-session.
4) Compare client-side token accounting (SDK counts + request payload) to Redwood Console per-request token attribution for the same API key and time window.
suspected_root_causes: Race condition in the per-request accounting path when runtime hot-reloads kernels -> duplicate emission of token accounting events
Streaming finalization path not always sending 'session_end' accounting event in older private agents (runtime < 1.20)
Batch attribution edge-case: when a batch contains both customer A and B and a fallback model is used, we sometimes attribute the whole batch cost incorrectly to the first request in the batch
Clock skew between customer-side SDK and Redwood metering aggregation can cause misaligned billing windows leading to apparent under/over counts in short windows
proposed_fixes: Hotfix (short-term): add a de-duplication guard in the accounting ingestion service that dedupes events by (request_id, customer_id, sequence_hash) for 5 minutes. Deploy to hosted and dedicated ingestion clusters ASAP.
Runtime patch (medium-term): make streaming finalization idempotent and emit an explicit finalized accounting event; bump private agent to 1.20+ with that fix.
Batch attribution change (design): change attribution logic to compute per-request token share using token indices recorded in kernel outputs rather than batch-level heuristics.
Metrics and alerting: create an automated diff check between per-API-key Console tokens and aggregated per-request ingestion counts; alert when >3% drift for 1 hour.
Billing reconciliation procedure: produce a reconciliation report for impacted customers with per-request evidence (timestamps, request_id, token breakdown, model variant).
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotent accounting events; simulate duplicated ingestion and ensure single accounting record is emitted.
Integration tests: replay production traces from affected customers through the patched ingestion pipeline and validate final counts match ground-truth tracer.
Canary: Deploy ingestion dedupe guard to 5% of traffic and validate diff alerts drop to <0.5% for canary customers over 48 hours.
Private agent rollout plan: staged upgrade with preflight metering smoke test (local replay) before agent upgrades in customer environments.
rollout_and_rollback: Rollout plan for hosted/dedicated ingestion hotfix: deploy to ingestion-canary -> ingestion-stable -> 100% within 8 hours assuming no alerts.
Rollback: revert dedupe guard config and reprocess any affected invoices if duplication was incorrectly removed. Keep a persisted snapshot of raw events for 7 days.
Private agent: provide agent 1.20+ patch release with clear migration steps; if customer sees disruption, allow pinned runtime-1.20-without-finalization-change until we collect logs.
monitoring_and_dashboards: New dashboard: per-API-key token-diff (Console tokens - ingestion tokens) with 1h/24h/7d views.
Alert: token-diff > 5% for 2 consecutive hours -> P0 paging to oncall billing eng.
Instrument: increase retention of per-request tracing from 24h -> 72h for affected clusters to assist reconciliation.
Create SLO: maintain token accounting drift < 1% across customers on hosted and dedicated for rolling 30d window.
customer_communications: Initial triage update sent to affected customers 2026-02-26: acknowledging discrepancy and committing to a reconciliation timeline.
2026-03-02: delivered first reconciliation artifacts for Customer-X (partial) and set expectation for final report by 2026-03-14.
Prepare template for finance-facing reconciliation report with per-request evidence and proposed credit adjustments.
